x_thread:
One canvas. Two operators. 🎛️

I built AgentFlow — a workflow builder where you and your browser agent operate the SAME machine.

You: drag modules, wire pins, press RUN → amber signals
Agent: add_node → connect_nodes → execute_workflow → cyan signals
Same wires. Same engine. No screenshots.

19 WebMCP tools declared by the page, mediated by the browser. Chrome (chrome://flags → WebMCP) + ChatGPT in-app browser.

No DOM scraping. No guessing buttons.

15 typed modules: API Call, Transform, Condition, AI, Delay… Grid-snapped, DAG-executed in topological order.

Runs in your browser. Autosaves locally. No signup.

Try it live → https://agentflow-hackathon.pages.dev
Landing → https://agentflow-landing.pages.dev
Source → github.com/Parithosh-Varma/agentflow-webmcp

MIT. Built for the WebMCP Hackathon.

Drag 15 modules, wire them, press RUN — or tell your agent 'Add an API Call and run it' and watch amber (you) → cyan (agent) signals march across the same wires. 19 WebMCP tools, no DOM scraping, runs in your browser.
producthunt.first_comment:
Hey hunters! 👋 I built AgentFlow for the WebMCP Hackathon.

Problem: Visual builders treat agents as second-class — agents must screenshot and guess buttons.
Solution: AgentFlow declares 19 structured WebMCP tools. Any WebMCP agent can add_node, connect_nodes, execute_workflow — same engine you use.

Try it with zero signup: https://agentflow-hackathon.pages.dev
Enable WebMCP in Chrome: chrome://flags → WebMCP → Enabled

Ask your agent: 'Add a GitHub API Call, connect it to Start, and run'
Would love your feedback!
